lesson.summary: Introduction to C: History, Characteristics and Classification
points: Dennis Ritchie developed C at Bell Labs in the early 1970s, building on B in the Unix environment.
C is general purpose, procedural and imperative; it is normally compiled.
Portability needs care with implementation-dependent behavior. Middle-level is an informal classroom label, not an ISO language category.

archive_evidence.era: The move to a new computer
archive_evidence.history: Unix moved from the PDP-7 to the PDP-11. The new machine's handling of individual bytes made weaknesses in B's word-based model more apparent.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: BCPL used an exclamation mark for indexing an array. B supplied bracket notation, which readers of C will recognize.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: C developed in the early 1970s. At Bell Labs, Ritchie built on B to create a systems language suited to the work on Unix.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: BCPL influenced B. B in turn influenced C. Early C carried over much of B's notation while adding a richer type system.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: The team needed a way to express systems software at a higher level than assembly. Work on a real operating system shaped the language as it evolved.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language
